minimal_repairs.subject: cor-cm-flow-domain-open-and-flow-is-c1
minimal_repairs.proposal: Use the norm convention supplied explicitly by repaired smooth-dependence theorem in F1/1.1, retaining the original Statement. In 1.1 define d_K(z)=min_{k in K}||z-k||2: k->||z-k||2 is continuous by reverse triangle inequality and K is nonempty compact, so extreme-value theorem gives the minimum. For a minimizer k_w, d_K(z)<=||z-k_w||2<=||z-w||2+d_K(w); reverse z,w to show |d_K(z)-d_K(w)|<=||z-w||2. Thus H={d_K<=delta} is closed. Compact K is bounded, choose B with ||k||2<=B; a minimizing k for z in H gives ||z||2<=B+delta, proving boundedness. Heine-Borel yields compact H. If complement U is nonempty, its compact-gap separation d>delta excludes H intersect complement U. If U=R^n omit only that separation argument, retaining closedness/boundedness. The operator-norm continuity above makes L finite on H. Remaining finite patching, reverse-time, endpoint and C1 statements remain unchanged.

published_local_use_context.used_clause: where $B\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is open, such that the components
premise_quotes: Here $T^n=\mathbb R^n/\mathbb Z^n$ has the quotient topology and the smooth atlas generated by the inverses of the restrictions of $q_n:x\mapsto[x]$ to open boxes whose side lengths are less than one. The map $q_n$ is open, since the preimage of $q_n(V)$ is $\bigcup_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}(V+k)$ for open $V$; its restriction to each such box is injective and a homeomorphism onto an open set. On each overlap component the chart transition is translation by a fixed integer vector, hence smooth. The quotient is Hausdorff and second countable as in [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]], so this atlas specifies a smooth manifold ([[def-smooth-manifold]]), and $q_n$ is a local diffeomorphism. The symbols $d\theta_i$ mean the global one-forms obtained from the differentials of these local lifts; integer translations leave those differentials unchanged. The product $A\times T^n$ carries the corresponding product charts.
